chunks: And Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, who said: Isma'il ibn Ishaq ibn Aban al-Warraq narrated to me from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), would raise his hand at the first takbir for the funeral prayer, then would not raise it again until he turned for the final salam.

And although these narrations have come down [indicating a specific practice], if a person were to raise his hands in all the takbirs, he would not be blameworthy for that, but rather he would deserve reward for it. And that which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Did Ali ibn Abi Talib raise his hands during all takbirs in the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq highlights the Sunnah of the first Caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib, who raised his hands only at the initial takbir during the funeral prayer, establishing a specific precedent. However, the text clarifies that this was not a restrictive prohibition; rather, raising hands in all four takbirs is considered permissible and meritorious, reflecting the Shia principle of flexibility (tawassu') in ritual acts where the text is not explicit. This distinction underscores the importance of following the Prophet's household's specific practices while acknowledging the validity of broader communal practices.
